To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
biodiversity enhances many ecosystem services and the loss of biodiversity substantially decreases ecosystem stability.

biodiversity loss substantially diminishes ecosystem functioning and stability and that the effects of biodiversity loss on these ecosystem services are most severe at the large temporal or spatial scales relevant for policy and management.
biodiversity loss substantially diminishes the benefits of ecosystems to people, especially at large spatial and long temporal scales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence and dependence between people and biodiversity across scales.
understanding how biodiversity influences and depends on people, and how these relationships can help us manage biodiversity and its benefits for people in a sustainable manner.
the link between the influence and dependence on biodiversity across scales of space and times.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biodiversity loss substantially diminishes the benefits that people obtain from ecosystem services.

biodiversity enhances the delivery of many ecosystem services, but the magnitude and nature of the relationship is context dependent, and that this relationship can be disrupted by human activity, particularly at large temporal and spatial extents.
biodiversity loss is likely to have a substantial negative influence on the provision of ecosystem services, especially at large temporal and spatial scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biodiversity loss has a substantial influence on people, but the magnitude of that influence depends on the spatial and temporal scale of the study.
we have shown how biodiversity can enhance nature's benefits to humans, and how the loss of biodiversity can diminish them.
we are currently developing a new framework for assessing human dependence on biodiversity across multiple temporal and spatial scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people's dependence on biodiversity is not only an important driver of biodiversity loss, but also a major determinant of the consequences of that loss.
the loss of biodiversity will have a large impact on the services people depend on.
the dependence of human societies on the services provided by ecosystems, and the influence of human societies on ecosystem services, are linked across spatial and temporal scales.
